rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=foe, bilateral_on_top=True, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.5, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 param_efficient breast. SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: iter-1 hr 0.2635 (3 epochs, reg barely engaged) BEAT iter-2 hr 0.1897 (11 epochs, reg fully engaged, train-loss monotonically down while val hr FELL). Diagnosis: the DC step is a GENUINE projector round-trip dc=R^T(Rx-g)/dc_norm, but with K=5 tied steps at weak alpha~0.09 five GD-DC steps cannot null the sparse-view streak residual, while the FoE+bilateral reg over-smooths every step -> the reg WINS as training proceeds. Data-consistency is the differentiator (coordinator: VN 0.63 @ 9k, LPD 0.68 -- genuine DC; image-domain-only caps ~0.28). Our DC is present but TOO WEAK relative to reg over K=5. (2) FAILURE MODE: under-consistency -- streaks survive because the GD-DC step size is too small to enforce Rx=g in 5 tied steps; reg dominates. (3) ONE KNOB: alpha_init 0.1 -> 0.5 (5x stronger DC/prox step). All else byte-for-byte iter-2 (train_n=200, K=5, FoE+M3 bilateral). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a 5x stronger step drives Rx toward g much harder per iteration, so the 5 unrolled steps actually remove streaks before the reg smooths them -> hr rises well past 0.2635, because DC-strength (not reg cleverness) is the sparse-view lever. Risk: too-strong alpha can diverge (dc_norm scaling keeps grad O(1), softplus keeps alpha>0); grad_clip=1 guards. ZERO extra params. (5) BUDGET: train_n=200 K=5 bs4 + 200-val, 1080s backstop -> <20min. (6) SERIAL; iter-4 self-dispatches (next: projection-domain filter ON -- sparse-view-native).
